subproblem.title: An integrable weight times a test form pulled back by a Lipschitz map is integrable (supplied step 3, third item)
subproblem.statement: Let Q, n ∈ ℕ, L ≥ 0 (NNReal), H : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q L-Lipschitz, S ⊆ ℝⁿ any set, g : ℝⁿ → ℝ integrable on S (Lebesgue measure), and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^Q) a test form (TestFormOn univ n: a smooth n-form with compact support). Then the function z ↦ g(z)·ω(H(z))(DH(z)e_0, …, DH(z)e_{n−1}) is integrable on S, where DH(z) := fderiv ℝ H z and e_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1 ∈ ℝⁿ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (Q n : ℕ) (L : NNReal) (H : Euclid n → Euclid Q) (S : Set (Euclid n)) (g : Euclid n → ℝ) (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid Q)) n), LipschitzWith L H → IntegrableOn g S → IntegrableOn (fun z => g z * (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid Q) n) (H z) (fun a => fderiv ℝ H z (EuclideanSpace.single a 1))) S
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent's supplied proof, third item (ŵ_i·f_{i,ω} is measurable and bounded by |ŵ_i|·sup‖ω‖·max(1, L_i)^{n+1}, hence integrable), stated for an arbitrary Lipschitz map H.
Notation. ℝ^m := Euclid m = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m) with Lebesgue measure volume. For z ∈ ℝ^{m+1}: z_0 := WithLp.ofLp z 0 and tail z := WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z)) ∈ ℝ^m. For t ∈ ℝ and x ∈ ℝ^m: ι(t, x) := WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x)) ∈ ℝ^{m+1}, so that ι(t, x)_0 = t, tail ι(t, x) = x and z = ι(z_0, tail z) (Fin.cons_zero, Fin.tail_cons, Fin.cons_self_tail, WithLp.ofLp_toLp, WithLp.toLp_ofLp). e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ ℝ^{N+1}; ê_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1 ∈ ℝ^{n+1}; e_b := EuclideanSpace.single b 1 ∈ ℝ^n; J x := ι(0, x) = WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons 0 (WithLp.ofLp x)) for x ∈ ℝ^N. DH(z) := fderiv ℝ H z, and DH(z)ê denotes the tuple a ↦ DH(z) ê_a. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α.

Proof. Put F(z) := ω(H z)(DH(z)e) = ω(H z)(a ↦ DH(z) e_a).
1. (ω is bounded.) ω is smooth (ContDiff ℝ ∞), hence continuous, and has compact support. So there is M ∈ ℝ with ‖ω(y)‖ ≤ M for all y ∈ ℝ^Q, where ‖·‖ is the operator norm of continuous alternating maps (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support). Since ‖ω(y)‖ ≥ 0, M ≥ 0.
2. (Derivative bound.) For every z ∈ ℝⁿ, ‖DH(z)‖ ≤ L (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz; at points where H is not differentiable fderiv is 0). Hence, for each a, ‖DH(z) e_a‖ ≤ ‖DH(z)‖·‖e_a‖ = ‖DH(z)‖ ≤ L, because ‖e_a‖ = 1.
3. (F is bounded.) By the operator-norm bound for continuous alternating maps (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm), |F(z)| ≤ ‖ω(H z)‖·∏_a ‖DH(z) e_a‖ ≤ M·Lⁿ for all z (monotonicity of products of nonnegative factors).
4. (F is Borel measurable.) For each a, z ↦ DH(z) e_a is measurable (measurable_fderiv_apply_const), so z ↦ (DH(z) e_a)_a ∈ (ℝ^Q)ⁿ is measurable (measurable_pi_iff). The map (x, w) ↦ ω(H x)(w) on ℝⁿ × (ℝ^Q)ⁿ is continuous: H is continuous (Lipschitz), ω is continuous, and evaluation of continuous alternating maps is jointly continuous (Continuous.eval / continuous_eval). Composing this continuous map with the measurable map z ↦ (z, (DH(z)e_a)_a) (both spaces are second countable, so the product carries the product Borel structure) shows that F is measurable, hence a.e. strongly measurable.
5. (Integrability.) g is integrable on S and F is a.e. strongly measurable with |F| ≤ M·Lⁿ everywhere, so the product z ↦ g(z)·F(z) is integrable on S (Integrable.mul_bdd applied to the restricted measure). ∎

Appendix (supplementary; the numbered argument above is complete without it). The following Lean proof of exactly this frozen statement was checked with `lake env lean` after `import GMT.Ch07.Submission`, inside `namespace GMT.Ch07` with the contract's opens and `noncomputable section`, with the declaration named Submission.X as in accepted nodes. Its axioms are propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only, and sibling theorems are referenced by their Submission. names.
Lean tactic block for `theorem Submission.cmcdt_lpi_cyl_pullback_integrable`, whose type is exactly the frozen lean_statement of this child (it follows `:= by`):
  intro Q n L H S g ω hH hg
  have hωc : Continuous (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid Q) n) := ω.2.1.1.continuous
  have hωs : HasCompactSupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid Q) n) := ω.2.1.2
  obtain ⟨M, hM⟩ := hωc.bounded_above_of_compact_support hωs
  have hmeas : Measurable fun z => (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid Q) n) (H z) (fun a => fderiv ℝ H z (EuclideanSpace.single a 1)) := by
    have hv : Measurable fun z => (fun a : Fin n => fderiv ℝ H z (EuclideanSpace.single a 1)) :=
      measurable_pi_iff.mpr (fun a => measurable_fderiv_apply_const ℝ H _)
    have hc : Continuous fun p : Euclid n × (Fin n → Euclid Q) => (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid Q) n) (H p.1) p.2 :=
      (hωc.comp (hH.continuous.comp continuous_fst)).eval continuous_snd
    exact hc.measurable.comp (measurable_id.prodMk hv)
  have hbd : ∀ z, ‖(ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid Q) n) (H z) (fun a => fderiv ℝ H z (EuclideanSpace.single a 1))‖ ≤ M * (L : ℝ) ^ n := by
    intro z
    have hM0 : 0 ≤ M := (norm_nonneg _).trans (hM (H z))
    have hcomp : ∀ a : Fin n, ‖fderiv ℝ H z (EuclideanSpace.single a 1)‖ ≤ L := by
      intro a
      calc ‖fderiv ℝ H z (EuclideanSpace.single a 1)‖ ≤ ‖fderiv ℝ H z‖ * ‖(EuclideanSpace.single a (1 : ℝ))‖ :=
            ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm _ _
        _ = ‖fderiv ℝ H z‖ := by simp
        _ ≤ L := norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz ℝ hH
    calc _ ≤ ‖(ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid Q) n) (H z)‖ * ∏ a, ‖fderiv ℝ H z (EuclideanSpace.single a 1)‖ :=
          ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm _ _
      _ ≤ M * ∏ _a : Fin n, (L : ℝ) := by
          gcongr with a
          · exact hM _
          · exact hcomp a
      _ = M * (L : ℝ) ^ n := by simp
  exact hg.mul_bdd hmeas.aestronglyMeasurable (Eventually.of_forall hbd)
proof_key_steps: A smooth compactly supported form is bounded: ‖ω(y)‖ ≤ M.
‖DH(z)e_a‖ ≤ ‖DH(z)‖ ≤ L for every z and a.
The integrand is Borel: fderiv is measurable, and (x, w) ↦ ω(H x)(w) is continuous.
An integrable function times a bounded a.e.-strongly-measurable function is integrable.

audit.reason: The exact statement allows arbitrary S and needs no differentiability assumption. Measurability of total fderiv, its global Lipschitz bound, and compact-support boundedness give a bounded measurable factor. Multiplying by the integrable weight proves the conclusion.
